source: NYISO real-time zonal LBMP & Moses South interface flow, Jan 2023 – Dec 2025
findings: Average Moses South flow went from 581.9 MW southbound in 2023 to 195.1 MW southbound in 2024, then 188.1 MW northbound in 2025.
That is a change of -770.0 MW between 2023 and 2025, and the yearly average flipped direction.
Share of days with net southbound flow: 88% in 2023, 58% in 2024, 31% in 2025.
The most southbound day was 2024-01-15 (1,777.0 MW southbound); the most northbound was 2025-11-15 (1,021.6 MW northbound).
Daily flow vs D · North congestion: very weak positive correlation (r = 0.13). The two barely move together.
Daily flow vs F · Capital congestion: weak negative correlation (r = -0.32). Days with more southbound flow tend to be days when congestion raised that zone's price more.
Daily flow vs J · New York City congestion: weak negative correlation (r = -0.33). Days with more southbound flow tend to be days when congestion raised that zone's price more.
Hour by hour the links are weaker: D · North r = 0.06; F · Capital r = -0.19; J · New York City r = -0.16.
cannot_conclude: A correlation between Moses South flow and congestion shows they move together, not that one causes the other.
Moses South carries all power flowing south from the North Country, not only Smart Path Connect, so changes in flow cannot be credited to that project alone.
A change between years cannot be pinned on one cause; weather, fuel prices, demand, outages and new projects changed at the same time.
data_notes: D · North: congestion is exactly 0 for all of December 2025 (average, minimum and maximum). This may be a data gap, so that month is not interpreted.
